headline: Analysis choices and evaluation depth alter reported effects across biological datasets
label: Evaluation Choice Robustness Audits
summary: Public reanalyses and benchmarks now show that analysis and evaluation choices can create, erase, or reverse reported biological effects.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is that reported biological effects depend on analysis and evaluation choices. Two optogenetics reanalyses apply censoring-aware survival models to public Neuropixels and striatal seizure data, using permutation, bootstrap, and leave-one-out checks to test robustness. A rich-club study in Alzheimer's EEG shows that null network construction and hub re-identification can create or erase apparent group differences. A proteomic co-abundance benchmark finds that method rankings shift with evaluation depth and that no method dominates. Null-matched efferocytosis scoring in stroke transcriptomes and a conditioned sequence model that predicts interferon-beta responses but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects follow the same emphasis on explicit, rigorous testing. This framing is dominant rather than universal across the set. What is new is the explicit demonstration that identical data can support different conclusions under alternative analytic choices.
